strengths: Point-in-time customer, product, behavior and conversion features can be constructed without using future outcomes.
Churn, purchase-propensity and 30-day customer-value targets can be generated from future windows.
The data contains measurable predictive signal for churn and purchase propensity.
Customer behavior contains clear unsupervised cluster structure.
Customer-product interactions support offline recommendation evaluation.
Generator-authored latent variables and final status fields were excluded from baseline model inputs.
Source inconsistencies discovered during ML preparation are explicitly handled rather than silently ignored.
limitations: The frozen source contains 122 pre-launch behavior rows and 2 pre-launch orders. Phase 7 filters these before ML use.
The frozen source contains 3 valid order-days without matching behavior-history days. Phase 7 preserves these conversions using outer-merge logic.
The observation horizon is only 90 days, so the CLV target is a 30-day forward value proxy rather than true long-term lifetime value.
The recommendation catalog contains 29 products, so recommendation results are useful for baseline engineering but not representative of a large real-world catalog.
Synthetic generator rules can create learnable relationships that may be stronger or cleaner than real-world relationships.
No real customer dataset is available for external distributional or out-of-domain validation.
The single-stage CLV regressor does not beat the zero-value baseline on MAE, supporting a future two-stage purchase-probability plus conditional-value approach.
An anomaly/fraud dataset was intentionally skipped because the source does not contain sufficiently authentic fraud-related signals.
real_world_validity_statement: Baseline performance on this synthetic dataset demonstrates engineering and modelling usefulness. It does not establish real-world production model performance or external validity.
